hook: CHIME finds a pulsar so bright that FAST could detect its pulses across the Local Group.
hook_turn: FAST could detect its pulses across the Local Group.

readout.label: Brightest pulse flux density, PSR J2108+5055

summary: Astronomers found PSR J2108+5055, a pulsar that emits sporadic bursts every 0.495 s, using the CHIME radio telescope. Its brightest pulse is far stronger than typical pulsar pulses, and the FAST telescope could detect such a pulse from the edge of the Local Group. The luminosity depends on a distance estimated from the dispersion measure, which carries real uncertainty.
title: Discovery of an Extremely Luminous Sporadic Radio Pulsar
